security_concerns_to_review: Cross-tenant visibility rules for get_for_tenant/2 (lib/letflow/service_catalog.ex): a global-scope entry is visible to any tenant; a tenant-scoped entry is visible only to its owner; a tenant-scoped entry owned by a DIFFERENT tenant must return the identical {:error, :not_found} atom a genuinely-missing service_id returns -- never a distinguishable forbidden/unauthorized shape (SVC-01 non-disclosure rule). Confirm the single-query-then-pure-in-memory-check structure actually enforces this by construction rather than by convention.

The GLOBAL-table divergence from docs/migration/decisions/0003-ecto-schema-strategy.md Decision B: service_catalog is NOT tenant-schema-scoped (no :prefix, not registered in Letflow.TenantProvisioning.tenant_scoped_migrations/0). Review whether this global, cross-tenant-readable single table introduces any information-disclosure risk beyond what the design's own R-Co-grounded justification (global-scope entries are referenceable by every tenant by definition; service_id is globally unique across tenants and scopes) already accounts for. Full reasoning is restated in the migration's header comment and Letflow.ServiceCatalog's moduledoc.

The cross-schema referential-guard query (Letflow.ServiceCatalog's private referencing_active_definitions/2 + query_referencing_definitions/2): iterates every tenant schema via Letflow.TenantProvisioning.list_registrations/0 (new read-only function added by this change) and runs a jsonb structural EXISTS query (never a LIKE-on-serialized-string, deliberately avoiding R-Co's own bpm_active_defs_for_service bug) against each schema's own process_definitions table with prefix: schema_name. Confirm this cannot leak one tenant's process_definitions.id values to a caller who shouldn't see them -- delete/1 and update_scope/2 are the only callers, and both are catalog-owner-level operations (no route wired yet, REQ-192), but confirm the returned definition_ids/tenant_ids in the error tuples don't constitute an unintended disclosure path once REQ-192 wires a route on top.

register/1's tenant-existence check (check_tenant_exists/1 in lib/letflow/service_catalog.ex) queries Letflow.Identity.Tenant directly by owner_tenant_id before insert -- confirm this existence check itself does not leak tenant-existence information beyond what the caller already legitimately knows (the caller is naming the tenant_id itself, not probing).

Database-level CHECK constraints (required_auth enum, timeout_ms range, scope enum, scope/owner-consistency) are the authoritative enforcement per REQ-191's acceptance criteria -- changeset-level checks in lib/letflow/service_catalog/entry.ex are advisory only. Confirm no code path bypasses Repo.insert/Repo.update (e.g. no raw SQL insert anywhere) that would skip the DB constraints.

The SVC-04 permissions (:ServicesRead, :AdminServicesRead, :AdminServicesManage, already shipped by REQ-069 in lib/letflow/api/authorization.ex) are named in Letflow.ServiceCatalog's moduledoc but NOT wired to anything here -- REQ-191 has no route layer. Confirm this module's moduledoc doesn't contradict those existing permission names (it doesn't invent new ones).
acceptance_criteria_for_reference: the service_catalog table carries the scope/owner consistency CHECK: an insert with scope 'global' and a non-null owner_tenant_id is rejected by the DATABASE, and so is one with scope 'tenant' and a null owner_tenant_id -- two explicit tests, not changeset-level validation
required_auth and timeout_ms are CHECK constrained at the database level: an insert with required_auth 'BASIC' is rejected, and so is one with timeout_ms 0 and one with timeout_ms 3600001

get_for_tenant/2 returns a global service to any tenant; returns a tenant-scoped service to its owner; and returns NOT FOUND -- not a forbidden error -- for a tenant-scoped service owned by a different tenant, so the two cases are indistinguishable to the caller (three explicit tests)
service_id is globally unique: registering the same service_id for a second, different tenant fails, even when the first is tenant-scoped
register/2 with scope 'tenant' naming a tenant that does not exist is rejected without creating a row

delete/2 of a service referenced by an ACTIVE definition is refused and the error names the referencing definition ids; delete/2 of an unreferenced service succeeds -- and a test confirms the reference check matches an actual SERVICE_TASK service_id attribute rather than a substring of the serialized graph, by registering a service whose id appears only inside an unrelated string in some definition's graph and asserting that definition does NOT block the delete

update_scope/2 narrowing a global service to tenant-scoped is refused, naming the conflicting tenant ids, when another tenant's ACTIVE definition references it; widening a tenant-scoped service to global is always allowed

Letflow.Definitions.ServiceScopeValidator.validate/3 works unchanged when handed a Lookup backed by this catalog: a definition referencing a service not visible to its tenant is rejected at activation, and one referencing a visible service activates -- with no change to service_scope_validator.ex itself, confirmed by git diff

result.summary: Full report: handoffs/WF02-REQ191-20260830/security-review-req191.md. INV-1 (global-table divergence, cross-tenant visibility in get_for_tenant/2, cross-schema referential guard, list_registrations/0, Lookup tenant_id capture): PASS -- get_for_tenant/2's single Repo.get + pure in-memory branch returns the identical {:error, :not_found} atom for a genuinely-missing service_id and a different-tenant-owned one, no entry data or distinguishable shape leaks on either branch; list_for_tenant/2 scopes at the SQL layer; the referential guard is Ecto.Query + parameterized fragment (no raw SQL, no string-interpolated schema name or service_id), read-only, and only reachable from unrouted catalog-admin functions; list_registrations/0 is a plain read-only Repo.all(Registration) and Registration carries no secrets. INV-4: PASS, no secrets in the diff. INV-7: PASS, zero Repo.query hits in the new code; the jsonb guard uses Ecto.Query/fragment with bound params. INV-8: FAIL -- lib/letflow/service_catalog.ex:407, delete/1 does `{:ok, _deleted} = Repo.delete(entry)`, a bare match that raises Ecto.StaleEntryError (Entry has no optimistic-lock field) if the row is deleted concurrently during the preceding sequential per-tenant-schema referential-guard query loop -- a real TOCTOU window, and a direct match for INV-8's own grep heuristic. Deviates from this codebase's own precedent (Letflow.Webhooks.delete/2 passes Repo.delete's result through a with chain instead of bare-matching it). Not a cross-tenant leak and not reachable via any route today (none exists), but INV-8 applies regardless since it touches external I/O directly, and every applicable invariant is BLOCKER with no partial credit. INV-2/3/5: NOT-APPLICABLE (no route/controller, no scripting surface, no lookup-by-ID endpoint in this diff). INV-6: satisfied by this report itself. Routed to rework: handoffs/WF02-REQ191-20260830/step-02c-rework1-elixir-dev.json. NOT forwarded to REVIEWER.
